summary: This Dockerfile creates a Ubuntu container with Zsh shell, Git, and curl installed. It then sets up Oh-My-Zsh with a plugin for SSH config suggestions, adds a sample SSH config file, customizes the shell prompt to show a whale emoji, and starts an interactive login shell when the container runs.

explanations.3: This tells the Ubuntu package installer to skip interactive prompts during installation — useful in containers where we can't answer questions.
explanations.6: The --no-install-recommends flag tells apt to only install the packages we explicitly listed, skipping optional dependencies to keep the image smaller.
explanations.11: After installing packages, we delete the package cache files to reduce the final image size — once installed, we don't need those cache files anymore.
explanations.14: We're piping a script downloaded from the internet directly into the shell to install Oh-My-Zsh, with --unattended to skip interactive prompts and --keep-zshrc to preserve our existing config.
explanations.18: The --depth=1 flag clones only the latest commit history instead of the entire repository history, making the download much faster and smaller.
explanations.20: This sed command finds the line that says plugins=(git) and replaces it with plugins=(git zsh-ssh-config-suggestions) to enable the newly installed plugin.
explanations.25: The printf command outputs multiple lines that will be written to the SSH config file — each argument becomes a line, including the empty strings for blank lines.
explanations.42: chmod 600 sets strict permissions on the SSH config file so only the owner can read it — SSH requires this for security.
explanations.45: We're appending a custom prompt to the Zsh config that includes a whale emoji and color formatting to make it obvious when we're inside a container.
explanations.47: The -i flag starts an interactive shell, and -l makes it a login shell so it loads all the profile and config files we set up.
